messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High rate of GPU OOMs on streaming-decode pool in us-west-2. 5xxs and request drops observed -> paging oncall
maria (oncall): seeing lots of 503s and `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in pod logs. Request drops spike around 22:14 UTC. Noticed many long streams with no max_tokens set.
leo (eng-runtime): confirming, backend logs show a flood of decode sessions with token counts > 20000 for a handful of routes. Looks like a client sent an empty max_tokens in ~batch request and our default went to unlimited.
sam (eng-sre): adding immediate mitigation checklist: 1) global per-request token cap at API gateway, 2) scale down concurrent decode workers on that pool, 3) enable fallback model variant (cpu/quant) for heavy sessions. Doing 1 now.
dory (support): flagged 3 customers experiencing truncated responses and dropped connections. Jordan, can you correlate which tenants saw highest error rates?
jordan (cs): pulling tenant impact – looks like two big PLG customers and one small integration. Customer A saw ~12% failed responses in last 30m. I pinged their SRE.
maria (oncall): deploy-bot, please run gate: set nginx header enforcement -> max_tokens=4096 for all streaming routes.
deploy-bot: started pipeline for runtime-config-update. Job 7821 queued.
leo (eng-runtime): while we wait for config roll, I recommend a hotfix in the router to drop sessions that exceed 8k produced tokens. Patch ready, need +1 from SRE to avoid flapping. Patch snippet:
```
if (generated_tokens > 8192) {
  terminate_stream("token_limit_enforced");
}
```
sam (eng-sre): +1 apply on canary to 3 nodes. Also I'm kicking autoscaler to add 6 nodes to the private GPU pool to buy time.
maria (oncall): applied canary patch to nodes gpu-decode-03..05. Monitoring.
leo (eng-runtime): logs show immediate reduction in OOMs on patched nodes (CUDA OOM events down ~70% on canary). Gateway cap still pending.
jordan (cs): Customer A acknowledged and throttled their integration on their side. They're happy with temporary mitigation but want ETA on full fix.
dory (support): collecting impacted request IDs for CS and security audit. Pushing list to shared drive.
maria (oncall): to confirm: actions taken = gateway per-request cap pending, canary token-termination patch applied, autoscaler added nodes, reroute policy enabled to move new sessions to dedicated lower-throughput cluster. Any further blockers?
leo (eng-runtime): one blocker: a single node reported `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then restarted — possible GPU driver stress. I'm spinning up diagnostics and isolating that host.
sam (eng-sre): isolated the host, removed from rotation. No impact on cluster capacity after scale-up.
maria (oncall): OK let's keep this as active incident. I'll stay on call for the handoff. Please add timeline notes and collect logs.
leo (eng-runtime): collecting full decode traces + KV cache sizes for sessions that tripped the cap. Will attach in postmortem.
jordan (cs): notifying customers of incident and mitigations; will send templated note and follow up with A PM.
dory (support): created internal ticket INF-4728 to track support actions.
maria (oncall): summary for now: runaway-generation due to missing max_tokens -> GPU OOM cascade -> request drops for some tenants. Short-term: per-request cap + token-termination patch + extra nodes + isolate bad host. Next steps: permanent API validation to enforce token caps, add pre-routing request size checks, and add test for max_tokens absent in SDKs. Assign owners?
leo (eng-runtime): I'll own runtime validation and test.
sam (eng-sre): I'll own autoscale/playbook updates and node-driver diagnostics.
jordan (cs): I'll coordinate customer comms.
maria (oncall): handoff to night oncall at 3123456900 UTC in 11m. I'll include this thread. If no regressions, we'll move to LATENT and PM. Thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
